title: Projective fixed schemes of split torus representations and separating cocharacters
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $T=(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-gm-ga], and $E\ne0$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] with a rational representation $T\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$, meaning a group-scheme homomorphism, where $\operatorname{GL}(E)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(E\otimes_k A)$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Suppose $E=\bigoplus_{\chi\in\Omega}E_\chi$ is a finite direct-sum decomposition into nonzero subspaces on which $T$ acts by pairwise distinct characters $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_m$. In the chosen splitting each character is the Laurent monomial $\chi(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\prod_{a=1}^r t_a^{n_{\chi,a}}$, with $n_{\chi,a}\in\mathbf Z$. Write $\mathbf P(E)$ for the projective space of lines [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. There exists a group-scheme homomorphism $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ such that the integers $m_\chi$ specified by $\chi\circ\lambda(t)=t^{m_\chi}$ are pairwise distinct. For every such $\lambda$, the subfunctors of $\mathbf P(E)$ fixed by $T$ and by $\lambda$ are represented by the same closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], namely
$$\mathbf P(E)^T=\mathbf P(E)^\lambda=\coprod_{\chi\in\Omega}\mathbf P(E_\chi)\ \subseteq\mathbf P(E).$$
Here fixed means fixed after every commutative algebra extension, not just by rational points. Choose a basis $e_i$ consisting of bases of the $E_\chi$, put $\chi_i=\chi$ when $e_i\in E_\chi$, and write $z_i$ for its homogeneous coordinates. Each standard affine open $D_+(z_i)$ is $T$-invariant. On this open the fixed subscheme has ideal generated by the coordinates $z_j/z_i$ with $\chi_j\ne\chi_i$. If $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ is any $T$-equivariant closed immersion of a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]
$$X\times_{\mathbf P(E)}\left(\coprod_{\chi\in\Omega}\mathbf P(E_\chi)\right)$$
represents both fixed subfunctors $X^T$ and $X^\lambda$, as a closed subscheme of $X$. Its inverse images on the invariant affine opens $X\cap D_+(z_i)$ are the fixed subschemes of those opens. Rank $r=0$ and the one-character case are included; in either case a trivial $\lambda$ is permitted.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138--139 (fixed functor); Theorem 12.12, pp.234--235 (character spaces); Lemma 13.51 and the following paragraph, pp.274--275 (separating cocharacter and restriction to a closed invariant subscheme). The explicit fixed ideals are the standard-chart calculation of that assertion.

proof.text: Write the exponent vector of $\chi$ as $n_\chi\in\mathbf Z^r$. If $r=0$, there is only one character, and the trivial cocharacter works. Otherwise choose $M\geq0$ bounding the absolute values of every coordinate of every difference $n_\chi-n_\psi$, and an integer $N>M+1$. Put $a=(1,N,\ldots,N^{r-1})$. For a nonzero difference $d$, let $h$ be its largest nonzero coordinate index (starting at zero). Then $|d_hN^h|\geq N^h$, while $|\sum_{b<h}d_bN^b|\leq M(N^h-1)/(N-1)<N^h$. Thus $d\cdot a\ne0$. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices] the monomial map $\lambda(t)=(t^{a_b})_b$ is a group-scheme homomorphism, and $m_\chi=n_\chi\cdot a$ are distinct. When there is only one character the separation condition is empty and the zero vector also gives an allowed trivial cocharacter.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, printed p.274; Example 13.50, p.274; Theorem 7.1, pp.138--139. Explicit universal-algebra chart calculation supplied by Q50.

proof.text: Fix any separating $\lambda$, and a basis as in the statement. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the finite nonempty basis index set: the $U_i=D_+(z_i)$ cover $\mathbf P(E)$, and $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}k[u_j:j\ne i]$ with $u_j=z_j/z_i$. For any algebra $A$ and $t\in T(A)$, diagonal action multiplies $z_i$ by the unit $\chi_i(t)$; hence it preserves the nonvanishing locus of $z_i$. The action on this chart is $u_j\mapsto(\chi_j\chi_i^{-1})(t)u_j$. These formulas determine the morphism on every chart by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-chart-ratio-extensionality]; they are identities after arbitrary algebra extension. For $\lambda$, the corresponding multiplier is $t^{m_{\chi_j}-m_{\chi_i}}$. Thus both actions preserve the whole chart, including over nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, printed p.274; Example 13.50, p.274; Theorem 7.1, pp.138--139. Explicit universal-algebra chart calculation supplied by Q50.

proof.text: Let $x\in U_i(A)$ have coordinates $b_j\in A$, using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Test its fixed condition on $A'=A[v_1^{\pm1},\ldots,v_r^{\pm1}]$ and the universal tuple $(v_a)_a\in T(A')$. It implies $b_j(v^{n_{\chi_j}-n_{\chi_i}}-1)=0$. If the exponent difference is nonzero, then $b_j=0$: multiply by a sufficiently positive monomial to obtain two distinct polynomial monomials with coefficients $b_j$ and $-b_j$. The coefficient definition in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and the localization equality criterion in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] show that this equality forces both coefficients to vanish (a further monomial multiple still has distinct monomials). Conversely, if all $b_j$ with $\chi_j\ne\chi_i$ vanish, every coordinate is unchanged for every $A$-algebra and every torus element. For $\lambda$ repeat the identical calculation in $A[v,v^{-1}]$: separation says its nonzero exponent differences occur at exactly the same indices. No evaluation at $k$-rational torus elements is used.

e\chi_i)$ in $k[u_j:j
e i]$. By the preceding equivalence, an $A$-point of $U_i$ is fixed for either action exactly when its coordinate homomorphism kills $J_i$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] this is exactly a point of $\operatorname{Spec}(k[u_j:j
e i]/J_i)$. The quotient and closed-immersion descriptions [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient, def-weil-closed-immersion] therefore give a closed subscheme representing both chart fixed functors, with ideal precisely $J_i$, functorially for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, printed p.274; Example 13.50, p.274; Theorem 7.1, pp.138--139. Explicit universal-algebra chart calculation supplied by Q50.

proof.text: Construct a global closed subscheme without appealing to a fixed-locus representability theorem. Put $B=k[z_i]$ with degree-one variables and $I=(z_i z_j:\chi_i\ne\chi_j)$, a homogeneous ideal. By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality], applied to the surjective graded map $B\to B/I$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, $Z=\operatorname{Proj}(B/I)$ embeds closed in $\operatorname{Proj}B=\mathbf P(E)$ (the chart-compatible polynomial-Proj identification is supplied by [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space]). Its chart over $U_i$ is obtained by degree-zero localization, by [def-pc-proj]. The kernel formula of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-quotient-chart-kernel] makes its ideal $J_i$: every generator of $I$ divided by $z_i^2$ is $(z_a/z_i)(z_b/z_i)$ with at least one factor of weight different from $\chi_i$, while $z_i z_j/z_i^2=u_j$ supplies every generator of $J_i$. Multiplying by homogeneous polynomials and dividing by further powers adds no other generators. Thus $Z\cap U_i$ is exactly the closed chart subscheme of step 4.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, printed p.274; Example 13.50, p.274; Theorem 7.1, pp.138--139. Explicit universal-algebra chart calculation supplied by Q50.

proof.text: The opens $Z\cap U_i$ with $\chi_i=\chi$ have coordinate rings $k[u_j:j\ne i,\ \chi_j=\chi]$. Their overlap maps are the usual ratios $u_{j/h}=u_{j/i}/u_{h/i}$ by [def-pc-proj], so they are exactly the standard charts of $\mathbf P(E_\chi)$ from [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Charts from different weights have empty intersection: on $Z\cap U_i$ the coordinate $z_h/z_i$ is zero for $\chi_h\ne\chi_i$, whereas intersection with $U_h$ would make it invertible. Hence $Z$ is a disjoint union of its weight-block open subschemes. The displayed chart identifications and their inverses glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], giving $Z\cong\coprod_\chi\mathbf P(E_\chi)$ with its stated embedding. Each component is also closed since its complement is the union of the other open blocks.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, printed p.274; Example 13.50, p.274; Theorem 7.1, pp.138--139. Explicit universal-algebra chart calculation supplied by Q50.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $x:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\mathbf P(E)$, choose a cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by principal affine opens mapping into the $U_i$. If $x$ is fixed after every algebra extension, its restriction to each of these opens is fixed: any algebra over the corresponding localization of $A$ is also an $A$-algebra. Step 4 gives a unique factorization there through $Z$. These local maps agree on overlaps, since the quotient-ring description of [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives uniqueness of a lift, and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Conversely, a map through $Z$ is locally fixed by step 4. After any algebra extension the principal opens still cover, and equality of the acted-on map with the original map follows from the same gluing uniqueness. Thus $Z$ represents both global fixed subfunctors, not merely their values on fields.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, printed p.274; Example 13.50, p.274; Theorem 7.1, pp.138--139. Explicit universal-algebra chart calculation supplied by Q50.

proof.text: Finally let $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ be the equivariant closed immersion in the statement, and set $F=X\times_{\mathbf P(E)}Z$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every algebra $A$, an $A$-point $x$ of $X$ lies in $F(A)$ exactly when $i(x)$ lies in $Z(A)$. Equivariance gives $i(t x)=t i(x)$ after every algebra extension. A closed immersion is injective on points valued in any scheme: locally a map into an affine quotient is uniquely determined by its composite into the ambient affine, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion], and uniqueness glues by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Hence $i(x)$ is fixed if and only if $x$ is fixed, for both actions. On $X\cap U_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ the immersion is an affine quotient by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the fibre product is $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i/J_i C_i)$ by the quotient universal property and the fibre-product definition. These quotient charts make $F\to X$ closed and show that their fixed schemes are precisely its inverse images. The chart and fibre-product arguments include empty $X$, $r=0$, repeated basis weights within a block, and the single-character case, when every $J_i=0$.
